consumer: game::handle_action's ACTION_MOVE_* dispatch site, which asks 'perform the registered east-move action and let the turn loop charge the tick' by calling avatar_action::move(u, m, dest_delta)
scope: the engine's own active input-dispatch path for the registered planar movement action (not an inventory or map reach)
decisive_source: src/handle_action.cpp::game::handle_action (ACTION_MOVE_*) — its body consumes the registered movement action and calls avatar_action::move(u,m,dest_delta), performing the move so the turn loop owns the tick
divergence: A wall (or other impassable terrain) one tile east: the real action returns moved==false and the avatar stays put having spent the keypress as the engine would, whereas a shortcut that directly writes avatar position east would place it inside the wall and skip the turn cost, exposing the wrong (non-action) authority
